metric: Knight (classic) smothered mates per 100 games, 5s + 0.05s per move
baseline_note: B = development settings: SmotherClassic true, SmotherBuildKnightCheck 16, SmotherCrushQuiet 3, SmotherCrushMoves 16.

experiments.title: Once-repeated positions on smother lines (merged engine)
experiments.question: The prover rejected smother lines through any position seen before in the game. Allow a once-seen position always (R2), or only after an escape with the escape budget (R1E). On the engine merged with upstream 88337401, with grid72's openings.
experiments.verdict: No gain: 2.95 (R2) and 2.66 (R1E) vs 3.12 per 100 pooled; the extra proofs are escaped more. The merged engine itself matches 1.6 on the same openings (3.12 vs 3.19 per 100, no losses).

experiments.title: Escape budget, confirmation
experiments.question: grid71's E3 (3 moves at 20% of the clock after an escape) on fresh seeds, with more games at Stockfish 2000-2600.
experiments.verdict: Not confirmed: 2.69 vs 2.75 per 100 pooled at 5+0.05, and 1.33 vs 1.73 against Stockfish 2500. With grid71, 2.79 vs 2.71 over 19,600 games per arm (z +0.5). The escape budget stays off.

experiments.title: Stalemate-aware construction
experiments.question: 77 of 96 draws in 38,600 games were stalemates by us at about +20. Score a stalemated defender as a draw in construction mode's evaluation (the quiescence search cannot see stalemate).
experiments.verdict: No effect: stalemates 14 vs 16, knight smothers 3.03 vs 3.19 per 100 pooled. The stalemates are swindles set up beyond the horizon (a loose defender piece checks until we must take it), not a blind spot of the quiescence search.

experiments.title: Escape budget
experiments.question: After the defender escapes a proven smother, the prover gets a large share of the clock for our next 3 moves (20% or 40% each).
experiments.verdict: No gain: 3.15 and 3.10 vs 2.94 per 100 pooled at 5+0.05. Its strong-opponent cells (z ~2) did not replicate in grid73.

experiments.title: Knight supply: keep our knights
experiments.question: Knights of ours at +8 (0 / 1 / 2) went with 0.48 / 3.65 / 6.07 knight smothers per 100. A bonus per knight (150 or 300 cp, up to two) from +2 and through construction keeps them.
experiments.verdict: Fewer knight smothers: pooled 2.58 (K150) and 2.10 (K300, z -3.1) vs 2.98 per 100, although the bonus did keep the knights (no knight at +8: 26% to 9-13% against Stockfish 1500). The knight link was correlation, not a lever.

experiments.title: Zugzwang-aware prover
experiments.question: The prover keeps a quiet move only if a checks-only smother would follow a pass, so it misses zugzwang. Skip that test when the defender has 4 (Z4) or 8 (Z8) replies or fewer.
experiments.verdict: No gain: 3.73 and 3.70 vs 3.92 per 100 against Stockfish 1500, 3.40 and 3.20 vs 3.40 against Maia-3. More smothers are proven (Z8 6.0 vs 5.15 proof games per 100) but fewer delivered (61% vs 76%): a defender with few moves escapes into a quicker plain mate.

experiments.title: Track B: build from +3 or +2
experiments.question: Start construction much earlier (from +3, floor +1.5, or from +2, floor +1), 200 moves.
experiments.verdict: No gain: 3.37-3.43 vs 3.50 per 100; keeping pieces harder (Keep 16, material 1/16) lowers it to 2.05. Draws at the 400-ply cap rise to 8-10% and the score vs Stockfish 2600 drops to 91-95%. The build-earlier direction is closed.

experiments.title: Trap prototype, decider
experiments.question: The harness plays the move whose Maia-3-weighted replies walk into a forced knight smother in 2 (probability at least 0.05), 6,000 games per arm on fresh seeds.
experiments.verdict: A small, consistent plus that never reaches significance: 4.07 vs 3.70 per 100 (z +1.0); with grid66 4.13 vs 3.69 (z +1.5). This is the ceiling of trap steering with an exact opponent model; stopped.

experiments.title: Trap prototype (harness)
experiments.question: In decided positions with at most one open square next to the king, the harness picks the move most likely (by Maia-3) to walk into a forced knight smother in 2.
experiments.verdict: P >= 0.05: 4.27 vs 3.67 per 100 (z +1.2); any safe trap 3.53. Traps arise in about 7% of games; decided in grid67.

experiments.title: Stall switch, replication
experiments.question: grid64's stall switch (take a near smother after N construction moves without a new low in open squares) on fresh seeds, 6,000 games per arm.
experiments.verdict: Did not replicate: S12 3.90, S24 3.63 vs 3.77 per 100. The baseline itself swings 3.0-4.3 between runs; SmotherStallAfter stays off.

experiments.title: Stall switch
experiments.question: A hybrid build with no new low in open squares next to the enemy king for N construction moves takes the near smother (N = 12, 24, 40).
experiments.verdict: S12 4.03, S24 4.05 vs 3.16 per 100 (z +2.0), but the baseline was at the low end of its range; replicated in grid65, where it did not hold.

experiments.title: Any-smother presets across levels
experiments.question: The any-smother presets (SmotherClassic false, SmotherGoal Near) against Maia-3 1100 and 1900 at 5+0.05, and at 3+2 against Stockfish 1500 and Maia-3 1500.
experiments.verdict: Any smother (mostly near): 72.8 per 100 vs Maia-3 1100, 66.1 vs 1900; at 3+2 69.7 vs Stockfish 1500 and 69.3 vs Maia-3 1500; knight smothers fall to 0.5-2.4. No losses. Documented as a preset, not a default.

experiments.title: Material-protecting defender, threat-aware
experiments.question: DefSee 1 with an exception: never prune a defender move whose piece then attacks one of our pieces.
experiments.verdict: Lower: 3.50 vs 4.31 per 100 pooled at 5+0.05 (z -2.65). grid60-61's Maia-3 gain did not replicate; SmotherBuildDefSee stays off.

experiments.title: Material-protecting defender vs Maia-3
experiments.question: DefSee 1 (the defender in our search skips moves that lose material by SEE, checks excepted) against Maia-3 only.
experiments.verdict: Maia-3 1500 3.83 vs 2.98 per 100 (z +2.1), Maia-3 1100 4.80 vs 4.70; one loss (pruned forks). Retested with a fix in grid62, where it did not hold.

experiments.title: Material-protecting defender
experiments.question: The defender in our search skips moves that lose more than N cp by SEE unless they give check (N = 1, 100, 300).
experiments.verdict: No clear gain: D1 3.40 vs 3.02 per 100 pooled (z +1.0); real games did not keep more defender material.

experiments.title: Confirmation: earlier switch and ArmGap
experiments.question: H40 (SmotherPartialAfter 40) and ArmGap 48 + KnightCheck 8 on fresh seeds, 6,000 games per arm.
experiments.verdict: Neither replicates: H40 3.23 vs 3.55 per 100 (z -1.0), ArmGap 48 + KnightCheck 8 3.64 (z +0.3). 1.6 stays the baseline.

experiments.title: Arming bonus (ArmGap)
experiments.question: Extra knight-route points while at most one square next to the enemy king is open, where an armed knight converts.
experiments.verdict: No gain: 3.41-4.03 vs 3.73 per 100 pooled; the share of one-open positions with a knight armed did not move (27.0% vs 27.2-27.8%).

experiments.title: Track B round 3: presets for all smother types
experiments.question: Presets on existing options: H40, SmotherClassic false (AK), and SmotherClassic false with SmotherGoal Near (AN).
experiments.verdict: Counting all smother types, AN gives 67.6 per 100 vs 6.8 for 1.6 against Stockfish 1500 and AK 42.8, with no losses; knight smothers fall to 0.8-1.7 vs 3.0. No setting beats 1.6 on knight smothers.

experiments.title: Track B round 2: trap steering
experiments.question: Spending strength on traps: among moves that keep the win, prefer those the opponent is likely to answer into a forced knight smother.
experiments.verdict: Trap steering lowers knight smothers (2.3 and 1.9 vs 3.2 per 100 against Stockfish 1500), also against human-like Maia-3.

experiments.title: Track B round 1: build earlier and longer
experiments.question: Spending strength: does starting construction at +5 or +4 (floor +3 / +2, 200 moves, material counting less) raise knight smothers?
experiments.verdict: No gain in knight smothers; draws rise from 0.4% to 6-8% (games hit the 400-move cap). Strength stays far above the floor (96-98% vs Stockfish 2600).

experiments.title: Decoy term in the main version (Track A)
experiments.question: Does rewarding the setup of Philidor's sacrifice (a piece ready to go to the last open square) add knight smothers at full strength?
experiments.verdict: No gain against Stockfish 1500 at 6,000 games per setting; the Maia-3 difference is within noise. Stays off.

experiments.title: Strength margin of 1.6 (Track B baseline)
experiments.question: How far above a 2600 opponent does 1.6 play? Track B may spend strength down to scoring 80% against Stockfish 2600 (10+0.1).
experiments.verdict: 99.8% against Stockfish 2600 and 99.0% against 3000 (0 losses): a large margin above the 80% floor.

experiments.title: Prep phase: keep the smother ingredients before construction
experiments.question: Does a bonus for keeping our knight and queen and the enemy's pieces and king-side pawns between +4 and +8 raise knight smothers?
experiments.verdict: No gain against Stockfish 1500; differences elsewhere within noise. Stays off.

experiments.title: Small neural network as the construction score
experiments.question: A 16-neuron network predicts knight smothers better than the hand score (AUC 0.968 vs 0.936). Does it give more smothers in games?
experiments.verdict: At x6 it ties the hand score; stronger settings give up material chasing the network and lose games. Off by default.

experiments.title: Learned linear model as the construction score
experiments.question: 17 hand features fitted to 4.5M positions (AUC 0.936) instead of the hand-written terms.
experiments.verdict: Peaks near x20, equal to the hand score. Off by default.

experiments.title: Aiming for knight smothers
experiments.question: 1.5 aims at any smother. What do SmotherClassic and the knight-route bonus (KnightCheck) give?
experiments.verdict: About 5-6 times more knight smothers; the basis of the 1.6 settings.

strength.title: Upstream Stockfish 88337401 merged into 1.6 (new net nn-684d0e60e71d) vs 1.6
Prover time in undecided positions off vs on
strength.verdict: The prover costs no measurable strength.

audits: 83% of knight smothers close the box with the defender's forced reply to a check in the final sequence (2,481 smothers).
In stalled won positions, a forced knight smother existed in 2 of 120 positions with one open square, even with a much larger prover budget.
One-move traps against the real opponent (Stockfish 1500) were available in 1 of 240 stalled positions.
The engine's expected defender reply matched the real reply 81% of the time in construction mode.
The opening barely matters: across 600 opening and colour combinations (25,308 games), an opening's knight-smother rate in one half of the games hardly predicts the other half (r = 0.05).

release.headline: Plays for the textbook smothered mate: a knight mates a king boxed in by its own pieces.

endings.note: Share of games, 5s + 0.05s per move. Knight = textbook smother; full = boxed king, other piece mates; near = all but one square boxed.
